item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The "dubbed plague trees" comment and the line about termination if you ask and the same if you don't seem really out of place. "Startlingly painful" also sounds way too colloquial. If you wanna talk about how much it hurts, give us a number or a comparison to other notoriously painful insect bites. There are several indices for measuring pain from insect bites.

It also seems like it would be easy to contain the tree by just dropping a concrete box on it. And once you've got it contained, you could easily move it by making it drop all fruits shortly after sundown by shaking it with some kind of machine (those even exist in the real world for harvesting some kinds of fruit), letting all insects die and then cutting it down.
Unless the insects are capable of burrowing through the ground or concrete to get to prey, but that doesn't match what's said about them just "attack[ing] anything that moves". Just throw a bobblehead figure or an RC car in there and keep them occupied.

Other than that, I feel like it's missing a lot of information about the insects themselves.
A description of the poison would make sense. Since there is some information about the insects, it should be possible to gather some dead ones for analysis.
How strong is the insect bite? With no other information provided, it's reasonable to assume that they're about as strong as normal insect bites, meaning that protective clothing would suffice. And if that doesn't suffice and the insects could bite through even that, then that's an important detail that should be mentioned.

item.title: There seems to be a loophole
item.content:encoded:
If the fruits start developing at sunrise and are good to go at sundown, and the bugs only live for at most 2 hours; why not enclose the tree with some sort of heavy duty mesh cage, and then have some teleoperated robots (no need to waste D-class on this job) work on getting the tree loose from the ground, and once the 2 hours mark goes by, remove the cage, and transport the tree to a more secure location before the next sunrise?

Is the area also under the effect of another SCP that makes night time not exist?

And even if that is the case, it might still be worth testing what happens if the tree is shielded from sunlight; or possibly even trained to a different daycycle by shielding it from natural sunlight and providing artificial sun-like lighting with gradually changing light and dark periods, making the light periods eventually much shorter and the dark periods long enough to transport it with less rush.

Er, no, actually, that's not what "containment" means. To contain a thing, that thing has to exist first. ;)

Besides, the Foundation is a bunch of pack-rats. The cases where they'd prefer to destroy rather than contain are very, very rare. Who knows what we might learn from such-and-such a Keter object in the future, to help us guard against other SCPs? Who knows how our attempts at destruction might backfire on us? It's usually safer to keep the thing around than to try blowing it up.
